issue.body:
This PR is a step towards enabling a first cache-level tiling for matmuls. Currently, it introduces a new tiling level that replicates the tile sizes of the distribution level. This should be no-op in terms of performance as the single iteration loops should be eventually removed. This will also allow us to minimize the cache impact when changing the distribution sizes.

Currently, we are testing this in the codegen pass. To have this working, we have to switch the padding strategy to peeling, as padding has some implementation gaps that are exposed when we introduce more loops in the loop nest. There will be code size changes but that's the only way to move out of the local minima we are currently stuck upon. Consequently, this is removing the padding strategy from codegen.

We should be able to introduce cache-level tiling in a similar way for DT + UK in follow-up patches.

issue.body:
The result of `getDyanmiSizes()` and shape sizes mismatch if the original input is partially dynamic. E.g., the former one can return "%c1, %x, %c4096", while the latter one can return "1, DYNAMIC, 4096". They mismatch in `getMixedValues()` method because the dynamicValues should only contain `%x` element.

Since that we have the original information in the encoding, we can assume that they are inferred to static values during setting encodings. We can fold empty op's operands to attributes if they are constants. It matches all the information we have in MaterializeEncodingInfo, and `PackOp::getResultShape` can infer the actual type.

Fixes https://github.com/openxla/iree/issues/15061
